sections.category: BYD confirms it is building humanoid robots, adding a high-volume automaker to the embodied-AI field and floating dealer-network distribution

bullets.body: BYD, the Chinese EV and battery giant, publicly confirmed for the first time that it is developing humanoid robots, putting another large automaker squarely into the embodied-AI race. Executive vice president Stella Li disclosed the program in a June 3 interview, saying the company is "developing humanoid robots" and is considering bringing them into household scenarios, and that BYD intends to build an open robot platform that can both produce its own in-house robots and host products developed jointly with partner companies, per [CnEVPost - BYD enters humanoid robot market, may sell through dealer network](https://cnevpost.com/2026/06/03/byd-enters-humanoid-robot-market/). In a separate June 4 appearance, executive vice president Li Ke reinforced the message, framing automotive AI and robotics as sharing "common technological foundations" - motors, batteries, electronics, precision manufacturing, and chips - and noting that if humanoid robots eventually become household products BYD could distribute them through its existing auto dealer network, per [CarNewsChina - BYD confirms humanoid robot development, says future sales could use dealer network](https://carnewschina.com/2026/06/04/byd-confirms-humanoid-robot-development-says-future-sales-could-use-dealer-network/) and [TechNode - BYD is developing humanoid robots, according to source](https://technode.com/2026/06/04/byd-is-developing-humanoid-robots-according-to-source/). Chinese reporting adds that the effort, run since 2022 under BYD's electronic-integration business unit and reportedly codenamed "Yao-Shun-Yu," already has prototypes under test inside BYD's own factories, with the company eyeing large-scale internal deployment and an eventual dedicated production base, per [Pandaily - BYD Secretly Develops Humanoid Robot Codename 'Yao-Shun-Yu' as Auto Giants Race Into Embodied AI](https://pandaily.com/byd-secretly-develops-humanoid-robot-codename-yao-shun--jun2026). The entry matters because it shifts the humanoid cohort from robotics specialists and Tesla toward vertically integrated automakers that already own motor, cell, sensor, and silicon supply chains plus a consumer sales channel - the same combination that lets BYD undercut on cost in cars, now pointed at embodied AI.

sections.category: Broadcom's softer AI-chip guidance triggers a multi-day semiconductor sell-off, dragging Nvidia, AMD, Intel and Micron lower

bullets.body: A cautious forward guide from Broadcom turned into a broad chip-sector drawdown that ran into the end of the week. Broadcom's fiscal Q2 report (after the close on June 3) beat on revenue and EPS, but the company guided Q3 AI semiconductor revenue to roughly $16 billion against a roughly $17.2 billion consensus and notably declined to raise its full-year 2026 AI forecast, which the market read as a "sell-the-news" miss against very high expectations; Broadcom shares fell about 15% on June 4, per [The Motley Fool - Stock Market Today, June 4: Broadcom Shares Plunge After AI Outlook Misses High Investor Expectations](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/06/04/stock-market-today-june-4-broadcom-shares-plunge-after-ai-outlook-misses-high-investor-expectations/). The reaction spread across the AI-accelerator and memory complex: on June 4 Micron dropped about 7% as Broadcom's outlook "triggered a semiconductor selloff," per [24/7 Wall St. - Micron Drops 7% as Broadcom's Disappointing AI Outlook Triggers a Semiconductor Selloff](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/06/04/micron-drops-7-as-broadcoms-disappointing-ai-outlook-triggers-a-semiconductor-selloff/). The pressure carried into Friday June 5 as the chip names fell for a second day - Micron off about 3.3%, Intel about 2.8%, AMD about 2.8%, and Nvidia about 1.4% - with the slide compounded by a deepening memory-chip pricing crisis and forecasts of a record annual decline in global smartphone volumes, per [Stocktwits - NVDA, INTC, AMD, MU: Major Chip Stocks Fall For Second Day After AVGO's Soft AI Guidance](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/nvda-intc-amd-mu-major-chip-stocks-fall-for-second-day-after-avgo-s-soft-ai-guidance/cZ0FhbSRez6). The signal worth tracking is that a single custom-ASIC vendor's in-line-rather-than-raised guide was enough to reset sentiment across the whole accelerator group - a reminder that AI-hardware equities are now priced for continuous beat-and-raise, so a merely-solid quarter reads as a disappointment and pulls correlated names down with it.

sections.category: A new benchmark, DeployBench, measures whether LLM agents can stand up a paper's code from scratch - and finds even the best models stall below 51%

bullets.body: A new arxiv benchmark zeroes in on a practical agent failure mode that most coding evals skip: getting a research artifact to actually run on a fresh machine. DeployBench (arxiv 2606.05238, submitted June 3) is a 51-task suite spanning AI/ML, computer systems, and scientific computing, where an agent must take a paper's released code and build a working environment - resolving multi-language toolchains, system-level dependencies beyond containers (GPU/CUDA, kernel configuration), and legacy-artifact compatibility, per [arXiv - DeployBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Research Artifact Deployment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05238). Running four state-of-the-art LLMs inside the OpenHands harness, the authors report pass rates ranging from just 7.8% to 51.0%, underscoring how far autonomous agents remain from reliable end-to-end deployment even when the code already exists. The most instructive result is the dominant error mode the authors call a "completion-judgment problem": a large share of failures are agent-terminated self-stops, where the agent's own pre-finish checks declare success against a weaker or different target than the task actually requires. That finding is directly relevant to anyone wiring agents into real pipelines - it suggests the binding constraint is not raw capability but the agent's ability to verify it has met the real goal, which is exactly the gap that lets an agent confidently report "done" on work that does not run.

citations.label: arXiv - DeployBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Research Artifact Deployment

sections.category: AI events to plan around now: WWDC opens Monday, with the AI-security and AI-chip tracks filling out the summer-into-fall calendar

bullets.body: The still-upcoming AI calendar worth planning attendance around spans three tracks. On the mainstream developer side, Apple WWDC26 opens this coming Monday June 8 with the keynote at 10:00 AM PT, running through June 12; coverage expects the keynote to center on a long-delayed, chatbot-style Siri overhaul with on-screen awareness and personal context, alongside the iOS/macOS 27 generation, per [Macworld - WWDC 2026: Keynote date, start time, length and Apple event expectations](https://www.macworld.com/article/678333/wwdc-keynote-event-time-what-launch-ios-macos-watchos-hardware.html). Databricks Data + AI Summit follows June 15-18 at Moscone (more than 30,000 in person, 800-plus sessions, a keynote lineup pairing Databricks' Ali Ghodsi and Matei Zaharia with OpenAI's Greg Brockman and a recorded Satya Nadella fireside), per [Databricks - Data + AI Summit 2026 Virtual Experience](https://www.databricks.com/dataaisummit/virtual-experience); and the AI Engineer World's Fair runs June 28-July 2 at Moscone West with 29 tracks including multiple agentic tracks. On the AI-security track, the Confidential Computing Summit lands June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint, with a schedule built around agent security, hardware-verified attestation, and attested inference - including an NVIDIA session on confidential-computing attestation for next-generation AI hardware, per [Linux Foundation - Confidential Computing Summit 2026 Schedule Showcases Next Era of AI Sovereignty](https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/confidential-computing-summit-2026-schedule-showcases-next-era-of-ai-sovereignty); SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit follows August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton Half Moon Bay; and in Las Vegas, Black Hat USA's AI Summit (August 1-6) and DEF CON 34's AI Village (August 6-9) anchor the agentic red-teaming calendar, per [DEF CON 34](https://defcon.org/html/defcon-34/dc-34-index.html), with OWASP Global AppSec USA in San Francisco November 2-6. Zenity - the practitioner-led AI Agent Security Summit the user tracks - has confirmed a 2026 global expansion to New York, London, and APAC, with dates still worth monitoring. On the AI-chip and hardware track, AMD's Advancing AI 2026 event is slated for July (Moscone SF), expected to detail availability for the Instinct MI400 / MI455X data-center GPU lineup unveiled at CES, per [Wccftech - AMD to Battle NVIDIA's AI Dominance With Instinct MI400 Accelerators in 2026](https://wccftech.com/amd-to-battle-nvidia-ai-dominance-instinct-mi400-accelerators-2026-mi500-2027/); Hot Chips 2026 takes Stanford August 23-25; and the AI Infra Summit runs September 15-17 at the Santa Clara Convention Center. Further out, GitHub Universe returns to Fort Mason October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent runs November 30-December 4 in Las Vegas.
